title: What does a tin can look like from above and from the side?
description: A tin can is a cylinder with a radius of three centimetres and a height of ten centimetres. The video finds the profile it shows from directly above and from the side. Keeko's doubt is that the rectangle is three centimetres wide.
teaching_notes: One idea: the profile is the outline seen from one viewpoint, and the width of the side profile of a cylinder is its diameter. Watch for students who use the radius as the width.

source: A tin can is a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. W
video_script.why: The child has met profiles in the book and now finds the two profiles of a cylinder with its measures.
video_script.substitution: Look from directly above to see the circle, then look from the side to see the rectangle, and find its width and height.
video_script.anchor: a tin can, a cylinder with radius three centimetres and height ten centimetres
video_script.wrong_answer: the rectangle is three centimetres wide
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the rectangle is three centimetres wide because the radius is three centimetres. The width goes right across the can through the centre, so it is the diameter.
video_script.payoff_line: A circle of radius three centimetres from above, and a rectangle six by ten from the side

final_answer.value: A circle of radius 3 cm from above; a 6 cm by 10 cm rectangle from the side
final_answer.spoken: a circle of radius three centimetres from above, and a six centimetre by ten centimetre rectangle from the side

hold_back: Answer: A circle of radius 3 cm from above; a 6 cm by 10 cm rectangle from the side
never_show: a rectangle 3 cm wide marked as right
maths_rules: from directly above you see the round lid: a circle of radius 3 cm
from the side you see the width and the height: a rectangle
the width is the diameter: 2 x 3 = 6 cm
slip: the width is not the radius 3 cm
video_script.design: A tin can stands on the stage; the view point moves above it and then to its side, and the outline of each view is drawn beside it.

<bookmark mark='tin'/>A tin can is a cylinder with a radius of three centimetres and a height of ten centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What profile does it show from directly above, and what from the side?

marks.given: the radius and the height are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the profile from directly above and from the side.

<bookmark mark='radius'/>The profile is a circle, with the same radius as the can, three centimetres.

marks.side: the view moves to the side of the can

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>Step two, look from the side. You see the width of the can and its height.

beats.on_screen: Width = diameter = 2 x 3 = 6 cm. Height = 10 cm.

marks.dia: the line is marked as the diameter and 2 x 3 = 6 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='width'/>Step three, find the sides of the rectangle. The width goes right across the can, through the centre. <bookmark mark='dia'/>That is the diameter, two times three, which is six centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Answer: A circle of radius 3 cm from above; a 6 cm by 10 cm rectangle from the side
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A circle of radius three centimetres from above, and a rectangle six by ten from the side.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the tin can
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows a rectangle 3 cm wide, struck through; the view from above shows the lid with the radius and then the whole diameter marked

marks.doubt: the bubble appears beside the side profile
marks.lid: the lid is shown from above with the radius marked and then the whole diameter marked
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the width 6 cm returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the rectangle is three centimetres wide, because the radius is three centimetres.
<bookmark mark='lid'/>Look at the lid from above. The radius goes only from the centre to the edge, so it covers half of the width.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The whole width is two radii. It is six centimetres.
